about: NEUSTRIA WEST: the port cards of Quentovic, Rotomagus, Parisius, Namnetis, Herio and Burdigala (Design/content/BRIEF.md, BRIEF_2.md), written 6 Oct 2026 by the weaver of the region from the six places files (Data/places/<port>.json), the dossiers and the spine. Every card names its port in 'when' (port.id) and is on its site's 'do' list in the places file. The people are the places files' people: each card's note says who, by id. Flags of this file begin nw_; the spine's thread flags (bs_, lf_, yk_, sv_, hy_, bk_, sx_, df_) are set only for the step the spine names. Small stories run between ports by flags: the abbot's psalter (Parisius, Rotomagus), the schoolmaster's books (Rotomagus, Quentovic), the exile's letter (Herio, Quentovic), the cooper's debt (Rotomagus, Parisius), the oil for three lamps (Burdigala, Herio), the poet's book (Burdigala, Namnetis), the nine and the chest (Burdigala, Namnetis), the clerk and the Bible (Herio, Namnetis). The words are in Data/writing/neustria_west.json: each option's note names the key of its outcome text, and art.<card id> says what the card's picture shows. A draft for the user to overwrite. (?) marks what could not be checked.

cards.note: People: quentovic.leofstan (the skipper), quentovic.wulfgifu (the host). The spine's hook for black_stones at Quentovic: an English ship under arrest, her wool rotting. Whether the ban of about 790 ever bit is disputed (Gesta abbatum Fontanellensium c. 12 against Alcuin, letter 7): the game lets it bite on one ship. Stops when the chain frees the ship (ch_black_stones_ship_freed) or the peace is heard (bs_peace). Wool sound is 8 d the sack (goods_793.json).
cards.when: moored and port.id = quentovic and year < 797 and not flag.bs_peace and not flag.ch_black_stones_ship_freed
cards.title: The sealed ship
cards.intention: An English ship lies roped to a post on the bank with the toll's seal on her hatch, by the king's order against English merchants. Her wool is spoiling under the hatch and her master counts the days aloud.

options.label: Lend him your crew for a day to turn and air the wool
Buy six sacks at a rotting price
Hear him out and tell him what wool fetches at Dorestad

memory.talked: told him the price of wool

cards.note: People: quentovic.hildric (the clerk); the Frisian is a forged shipmaster. An oath: a free man charged without proof clears himself by his own oath and those of oath-helpers of his standing (Frankish practice in the capitularies and the Lex Salica; the number of helpers here is the game's (?)). The helpers swear to the man, not to the fact. The chance is whether the player judged him right.
cards.when: moored and port.id = quentovic and year < 827 and port.visits > 0
cards.title: Two to swear with him
cards.intention: At the toll house a Frisian shipmaster is charged with declaring thirty bolts of cloth and landing forty. He may clear himself by oath if two men of his own trade swear that his oath is good, and he has found one.

options.label: Swear with him
Ask the clerk to count the bolts again before anyone swears
Say you do not know him well enough

memory.swore: swore beside a Frisian at the toll
memory.counted: asked for a count before an oath
memory.refused: would not swear for a stranger

cards.note: People: quentovic.gerwin (the moneyer); rotomagus.moneyer is his sister's son (flag nw_gerold_word, set at Rotomagus). The spine's hook for silver_road at Quentovic: the Channel mint, where English pennies go into the pot and come out Frankish. The heavy penny and the order that it be taken everywhere: Synod of Frankfurt 794 c. 5 (chronicle_793.json 794-06-frankfurt-new-denier). The loss on foreign coin is the game's (trade_rules.json foreign_loss 0.1): four in forty, two when sorted.
cards.when: moored and port.id = quentovic and year >= 794 and year < 816 and silver >= 40
cards.title: The moneyer's pot
cards.intention: Only the king's new heavy penny passes now. The moneyer takes old and foreign silver into his pot and gives back new pennies, less his cut, and he cuts less for silver that comes to him sorted.

options.label: Spend the evening sorting it first: good from doubtful, English from old
Tip the purse out as it is
Slip one light penny in, to see whether he is as good as he says
Keep your silver and ask what the king has ordered about the coin

memory.tested: tried him with a light penny

cards.note: A rumour that is not true. Invented, in the manner of the years after 793: every coast heard of Lindisfarne as fast as a ship and no faster, and every low hull was a raider for a season. Both outcomes of sailing show the truth (herring boats from Boulogne). The first recorded attack on Quentovic is 842 (Annales Bertiniani; Nithard): the card stops before it. The price word at Dofras is true: one wine keel in a week is short supply.
cards.when: moored and port.id = quentovic and year < 842 and month >= 5 and month <= 9
cards.title: Sails off the bar
cards.intention: On the long street a wine seller is telling everyone that heathen ships lie off the river mouth. The pilots have stopped taking boats over the bar, and three masters have decided to wait.

options.label: Sail on the ebb anyway
Find out who saw them
Wait three days with the rest

cards.note: People: quentovic.meginbert (Saint-Germain's monk); herio.natalis keeps the next leaf. A riddle given: the spine's hook for riddle_road at Quentovic (a monk on his abbey's business with Aldhelm's salt; riddles_793.json riddle_aldhelm_19_salis, 12 d, the first of the set salt_to_pepper). The clues are our own rendering of Aldhelm, Enigma 19. Sets nw_salt_answered, which the Herio card does not need (it reads the riddle's own state).
cards.when: moored and port.id = quentovic and year < 819
cards.title: Once I was water
cards.intention: Saint-Germain's monk on the abbeys' row sells wine by the cask and riddles by the leaf. One leaf is Bishop Aldhelm's, in Latin, and he says it is the first of four.

options.label: Buy the leaf
Give him the answer
Set him a riddle of your own
Not today

memory.traded: set him a riddle he could not answer

cards.note: People: quentovic.meginbert; herio.natalis and herio.cellarer (Vitalis) are named. A commission: bay salt for Saint-Germain's fish, brought here from Herio or Namnetis (the tie in both files: Meginbert buys the island's salt). Saint-Germain's freedom from the toll at Quentovic: Charles's charter of 27 March 779. Salt is 3 d the sack (goods_793.json); the premium is the abbey's hurry.
cards.when: moored and port.id = quentovic and year < 819 and month >= 4 and month <= 9
cards.title: Salt for the abbey's fish
cards.intention: Saint-Germain's man needs bay salt for the abbey's fish before the autumn, and his usual carrier has not come back from the south.

options.label: Take the order: ten sacks before Michaelmas
Take it, and ask for a cask of the abbey's wine on account
Tell him what salt fetched at Dorestad, and leave it

memory.haggled: took the salt order and a cask on account

cards.note: People: quentovic.osmund (the guest-master); the cleric waiting to cross is forged. A fast day. The cell of Saint Josse was given to Alcuin 'to give alms to pilgrims' and cared for 'those from over the sea and other poor' (Lupus of Ferrieres, letters 11 and 71, as in the dossier). The porter's 'Thanks be to God' is the Rule of St Benedict c. 66. The famine: chronicle_793.json 793-spring-false-grain (the hungry years, to 794). The ship riddle is Symphosius 13 (riddles_793.json riddle_symphosius_13_navis; reward rw_tip_quentovic), given by 'a cleric waiting to cross', as the spine's hook asks.
cards.when: moored and port.id = quentovic and fast and year < 813
cards.title: A fast day at the cell
cards.intention: It is a fast day. The cell of Saint Josse feeds whoever is waiting on the wind, on fish, pulses and bread, and the guest hall is full.

options.label: Give a barrel of herring to the kitchen
Leave six pennies for pulses
Sit down to the fast with them and take the cleric's riddle

memory.fish: gave herring on a fast day
memory.sat: kept the fast in the guest hall

cards.note: People: cast.sigewine (the monk), quentovic.osmund (the guest-master); cast.alcuin, cast.higbald named. A passenger to carry, and a text given. The spine's hook for holy_island at Quentovic: Sigewine waits at Alcuin's hospice with Alcuin's answer and a small bag of the king's alms for ransom (?), looking for a ship north. Sets lf_knows_boys (the spine: 'set at Lindisfarena or by cast.sigewine'). Alcuin's promise to speak to King Charles for the boys is in his letter to Higbald (MGH Epistolae IV no. 20); the alms bag is the spine's (?). The text is alcuin_793 (Alcuin to King Aethelred), retold and not quoted.
cards.when: moored and port.id = quentovic and year < 805 and not flag.nw_sigewine_carried
cards.title: The bag and the answer
cards.intention: At the cell a tall English monk has been turning ships down for a month. He carries a letter from Alcuin for the bishop of the holy island and a small bag of alms to buy back the boys the heathen carried off. He needs a ship going north, and he is afraid of ships.

options.label: Take him to Dorestad, where the Frisian ships go north
Ask to hear what his master wrote about the raid
Tell him which Frisian masters go north, and when

memory.carried: carried him to Dorestad with the bag
memory.told: named him ships for the north

cards.note: People: Putul (real: Alcuin's deacon, sent home from York with Liudger and the Frisian merchants, Altfrid, Vita Liudgeri I.12; that he is a priest in Gaul by the 790s is the spine's (?)); cast.liudger, cast.ecgwulf, cast.thiadburg named or meant. A rumour that is true. The spine's easter egg for york_blood at Quentovic. Sets yk_feud_known. The killing at York about 773: Altfrid I.11-12. That no blood-price was paid is the game's (the spine).
cards.when: moored and port.id = quentovic and year < 805 and not flag.yk_feud_known
cards.title: The old deacon
cards.intention: An old English priest who says Mass at the cell some Sundays was at York twenty years ago, when a Frisian merchant killed a nobleman's son and every Frisian in the city took ship for home. He was on that ship.

options.label: Ask who struck the blow, and whose son he killed
Ask after Liudger and his books
Leave the old man to his office

cards.note: People: quentovic.wulfgifu (the host); the priest of Saint Peter's is forged. A funeral. English pilgrims for Rome landed at Quentovic (Bede on Theodore, 668; Boniface; the letter of 796 on true pilgrims, chronicle 796-spring-offa-letter): the card runs from the peace of 796. The host who answers for a guest kept three nights is the Kentish law of Hlothhere and Eadric c. 15 (wording to check (?)).
cards.when: moored and port.id = quentovic and year >= 796 and year < 842 and month >= 5 and month <= 10
cards.title: Six to carry
cards.intention: An English pilgrim bound for Rome has died in the ale-house, waiting for his party. He is to be buried at Saint Peter's this evening, and there are not enough men in the street who knew him to carry the bier.

options.label: Carry him with your crew
Pay for the wax and a Mass
Offer to see his bundle and the news across to his wife at Dofras

memory.carried: carried a dead pilgrim to his grave
memory.bundle: took a dead man's bundle home

cards.note: People: quentovic.wulfgifu (the host), quentovic.leofstan named; the hand is forged. A hire. English merchants and shipmen lived at the wic (the dossier); her house runs to 842 under her daughter. The price word (wine short on the Kentish side) is true while it lasts.
cards.when: moored and port.id = quentovic and year < 823
cards.title: Wulfgifu's fire
cards.intention: Wulfgifu keeps the house where the men from over the sea lodge, and answers to the toll for every guest. By her fire sits a Kentish hand who was put ashore here and wants a berth on anything that sails.

options.label: Take the hand on
Stand the bench a round and listen
Sit by the fire and say little

memory.hired: hired an English hand from her bench

cards.note: People: quentovic.osmund; rotomagus.schoolmaster (Harduin) sent the asking (flag nw_borrowed_books, set at Rotomagus). The tie is in both files: Osmund borrows books from Saint-Wandrille's school and is slow to send them back. A book is 360 d (goods_793.json) and can spoil at sea (crew.cargo.book). The book with the whale is not named: a Physiologus or a saint's voyage would both have one (?).
cards.when: moored and port.id = quentovic and flag.nw_borrowed_books and not flag.nw_books_aboard and year < 812
cards.title: The schoolmaster's books
cards.intention: Osmund has two of Saint-Wandrille's books on his shelf, lent by the schoolmaster there and long overdue. The schoolmaster has asked for them by your boat.

options.label: Take the one and leave him his whale
Take both: a loan is a loan
Give him until you next call

memory.both: took both books, whale and all
memory.later: gave him time with the books

cards.note: People: quentovic.corbie_agent (Theudold, invented), herio.adalard (the exile), quentovic.hildric (the clerk). The second step of the Herio story herio.emperors_cousin: Adalard of Corbie, exiled on Herio 814-821 (Cartron 2010; Poupardin 1905), sends a letter to Corbie by Quentovic and has a small book brought back (the game's; his 'statutes' for Corbie are of 822). Comes only after the Herio card sets nw_adalard_letter. A book is 360 d: it may be sold, and then the Herio card says so.
cards.when: moored and port.id = quentovic and year >= 814 and year < 822 and flag.nw_adalard_letter and not flag.nw_adalard_book and not flag.nw_adalard_done
cards.title: Corbie's man
cards.intention: Corbie's man on the abbeys' row takes the exile's letter without surprise. In eight days he is back from the Somme with a book the length of a hand, sewn in oiled linen.

options.label: Take the book south
Take it, and let the toll clerk look at it first
Tell him the letter was all you agreed to

memory.clerk: showed the abbot's book to the toll

cards.note: People: quentovic.grippo (real: prefect of the emporium, Miracula sancti Wandregisili c. 15, about 858; his years beyond that are a guess (?)); rotomagus.einold sends him word. The edict of Pitres, 864, c. 25: death for selling mail, arms or horses to Northmen (MGH Capit. II no. 273). Before 864 the line about the edict does not show. His storm and his vow paid on Christmas Eve: the Miracula.
cards.when: moored and port.id = quentovic and year >= 858 and year < 871
cards.title: The prefect's question
cards.intention: Grippo, the king's prefect of the port, asks every master the same thing: whether there is a blade, a mail coat or a horse aboard that might find its way to a Northman.

options.label: Open the hold and let his men look
Tell him what sails you have seen, and where
Swear there is nothing, and keep the hatch shut

memory.swore.failure: caught with arms under the hides

cards.note: People: the Saxon is forged (the story rotomagus.weser_man); the wright of the slip is the port's; cast.crew.brunger is named in the outcome. A passenger to carry. The spine's hook for saxon_end at Rotomagus, 804-815: Saxon families set down on abbey land, a man asking for the Weser. The deportation of 804: Annales regni Francorum 804; that any were settled by Rouen is the spine's (?). Sets sx_carried_fugitive (the king's men may learn of it) or nw_weser_wright.
cards.when: moored and port.id = rotomagus and year >= 804 and year < 815 and not flag.sx_carried_fugitive and not flag.nw_weser_wright
cards.title: The man who asks for the Weser
cards.intention: At dusk a man comes down to the strand from the row of huts on the abbey's land. He is one of the king's Saxons, moved here with his people and a priest set over them. He asks whether any ship goes to the Weser.

options.label: Take the four aboard at night, for the IJssel and the road east
Speak for him at the slip, where the wright needs hands
Tell him truly that no ship here goes so far

cards.note: People: rotomagus.tollman (Angilwin; the same man as the arrival card harbour.tollman.frankish, whose memory these lines read), cast.gervold named. The spine's hook for black_stones at Rotomagus (before 797 he tells what the quarrel is, as far as a tollman is told; sets bs_ban_heard, 'told of the ban by someone who enforces it'). Gervold 'dearest friend' of Offa and the letters in the abbey's chest: Gesta abbatum Fontanellensium c. 12. The line about the Saxons answers this file's weser_man.
cards.when: moored and port.id = rotomagus and year < 813 and port.visits > 0
cards.title: Angilwin's chalk
cards.intention: The toll man at the river gate chalks every cask himself and cannot be hurried. Three boats are waiting on him, and the flood is making.

options.label: Wait your turn
Ask him why the ports are shut to the English
Hold his tally sticks and call the casks for him

memory.waited: waited his turn at the gate

cards.note: People: rotomagus.ursio (the cooper), parisius.waldric (who owes him; the tie is in both files), rotomagus.adalsind named. A deal and a favour: his word carried to the cellarer at the fair (flag nw_ursio_debt; the Parisius card harbour.parisius.skins_by_the_bundle sets nw_ursio_paid). Wine is 50 d the cask (goods_793.json); his cask is a buyer's leaving.
cards.when: moored and port.id = rotomagus and year < 816
cards.title: The cooper's mallet
cards.intention: The cooper in the market place knocks on a cask without being asked, listens, and tells the owner what is wrong with it. He is owed money upriver and has a cask to sell.

options.label: Buy the sound cask a buyer left with him
Promise to say his name to the cellarer at the fair
Take the cask he kept for you
Ask which cellar's wine is sound this year

memory.bought: bought a cask he vouched for
memory.word: took his word to the cellarer
memory.gift: had a cask from him in thanks

cards.note: People: rotomagus.hildhard (canon and chief singer). A riddle and a text given: Symphosius 5, the chain (riddles_793.json gives it to 'a cleric of the archbishop' here; texts_793.json symphosius_05_catena), in our own rendering. The story rotomagus.school_books: he teaches what a book is worth (sets bk_knows_worth).
cards.when: moored and port.id = rotomagus and year < 812
cards.title: Good day, in a riddle
cards.intention: A canon of the cathedral, its chief singer, greets strangers with a riddle in place of good day. He writes it on a wax tablet for anyone who cannot answer, and for anyone who can.

options.label: Take the tablet
Answer him
Ask him what a book is worth

memory.tablet: took his riddle on a tablet
memory.worth: asked what a book is worth

cards.note: People: rotomagus.hildhard, parisius.fardulf (who asks: flag nw_psalter_asked, set at Parisius), rotomagus.schoolmaster named. The tie is in both files: Hildhard owes Saint-Denis a psalter borrowed nine years ago and knows exactly where it is. A book is 360 d; the Parisius card harbour.parisius.abbots_psalter ends it.
cards.when: moored and port.id = rotomagus and flag.nw_psalter_asked and not flag.nw_psalter_aboard and not flag.nw_psalter_home and year < 812
cards.title: Nine years of psalms
cards.intention: The abbot of Saint-Denis has asked, by your boat as by every boat, for the psalter the cathedral's chief singer borrowed nine years ago.

options.label: Ask for it plainly, in the abbot's name
Pay for skins, so the boys can copy what they need first
Leave it with him and tell the abbot it is in use

memory.took: took the psalter from his choir
memory.copy: paid for a copy before taking the psalter

cards.note: People: the brother at the gate of Saint Peter's and the man in the row are forged. The spine's hook for hungry_years, 'also at Rotomagus': the abbeys feed the poor, and men tell of the false grain (chronicle_793.json 793-spring-false-grain; Annales Mosellani 793 (?)). The king's price for rye, three pennies the measure, is of Frankfurt, June 794 (the label says 'the monk's price' so that it holds for 793 too). The law of 805-806 against carrying food out of the realm: the capitulary of Thionville. Sets hy_fed_poor.
cards.when: moored and port.id = rotomagus and (year < 795 or (year >= 805 and year < 808))
cards.title: The table at the gate
cards.intention: It is a hungry year. Outside the wall the brothers of Saint Peter's ladle pottage at a table by their gate, and the row before it reaches the old graves.

options.label: Give two sacks of rye to the table
Sell him two sacks at the monk's price
Leave five pennies for the pot
Stand by the row a while and listen

memory.sold: sold rye at the monk's price

cards.note: People: rotomagus.adalsind (the ale-wife), hamwic.leofstan and quentovic.leofstan named apart (two men of one name: the tie in the Quentovic file). A rumour that is true: wine is dear over the sea until Christmas (the port's seasons; the price word at Hamwic is real while it lasts). The king's complaint of the short cloaks: Notker, Gesta Karoli I.34 (Grant 1907), retold, and Charles's letter to Offa of 796.
cards.when: moored and port.id = rotomagus and year < 823
cards.title: A stick on Adalsind's wall
cards.intention: Adalsind keeps the ale-house inside the river gate and a notched stick for every shipman who ever drank there. She knows who is in harbour and what wine fetched at the fair before the toll man does.

options.label: Pay what is notched
Ask what wine is fetching over the sea
Drink on the stick and settle next time

memory.asked: asked the price of wine over the sea

cards.note: People: rotomagus.moneyer (Gerold), quentovic.gerwin (his mother's brother; flag nw_gerold_word is read by the Quentovic card harbour.quentovic.gerwin_pot). The spine's hook for silver_road, 'also at Rotomagus', and its flag sv_first_dirham ('he has held a dirham and been told what it is'). A dirham on the Seine in the 790s is early: the stream into the Baltic is from about 800, and the game brings one stray coin south in a Dane's purse (?). No moneyer of Rouen is named in these years.
cards.when: moored and port.id = rotomagus and year >= 794 and year < 825
cards.title: The moneyer's tray
cards.intention: The young moneyer at Rotomagus keeps a private tray of every strange coin he was meant to melt. One of them is thin broad silver with writing like bird tracks and no king's face.

options.label: Tell him what it is
Hold it, and ask what the Dane said
Promise to carry his word to the Canche

memory.named: told him what the strange coin was
memory.word: took his word to his uncle

cards.note: People: rotomagus.schoolmaster (Harduin; real, died 811: Gesta abbatum Fontanellensium c. 12, checked at fr.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gervold), quentovic.osmund (who has his books), parisius.waldric named. A commission. The spine's hook for book_road at Rotomagus (Saint-Wandrille's new school and the books Gervold gave it; Saint-Denis buys parchment by the bundle at the October fair). Parchment is 60 d the bundle of a hundred leaves (goods_793.json). Sets nw_borrowed_books for the Quentovic card.
cards.when: moored and port.id = rotomagus and year < 812
cards.title: Skins for the school
cards.intention: A tide below the city, at Saint-Wandrille's landing, the master of the abbot's new school wants calfskin for his boys and his books, and has two books out on loan that have not come home.

options.label: Take his order: four bundles from the fair
Sell him the parchment you carry
Promise to ask Osmund for the books
Let him check your reckoning

memory.order: took the school's order for parchment

cards.note: People: rotomagus.schoolmaster, quentovic.osmund. Ends the small story of the borrowed books (flags nw_borrowed_books, nw_books_aboard, nw_books_all). Sets the spine's bk_carried ('carried a book safely for a church') or bk_lost ('a book in his care was lost').
cards.when: moored and port.id = rotomagus and flag.nw_books_aboard and not flag.nw_books_home and year < 812
cards.title: Books come home
cards.intention: The schoolmaster of Saint-Wandrille has seen your boat from the jetty and is already walking down, with his hands washed.

options.label: Hand over a book
Hand over both books
Tell him the books are gone

memory.home: brought a borrowed book home dry

cards.note: People: rotomagus.einold (invented clerk), namnetis.gunhard (his letter: flag nw_einold_letter, read by the Namnetis card), quentovic.grippo and cast.asulf named in the files. The spine's hook for dorestad_falls at Rotomagus: sacked 14 May 841 (Annales Bertiniani 841; the chronicle of Fontenelle); Oissel 858 (Annales Bertiniani). Ransoming captives is the deed bought_captives (reputation_793.json: ransom and redemption).
cards.when: moored and port.id = rotomagus and year >= 841 and year < 880
cards.title: The clerk's list
cards.intention: A clerk of the cathedral keeps a list of everyone carried off from the city since the fire, and what was last heard of each. He asks one thing of every shipman who goes north: to carry a name and ask after it.

options.label: Take a strip north
Put twenty pennies in the ransom chest
Take his letter for the bishop at Nantes
Tell him what fleets you have seen, and where

memory.word: brought true word of the fleets

cards.note: People: the quartermaster is forged (a Dane of the Seine fleets); rotomagus.einold stands by with the ransom chest. The spine's hook for dorestad_falls at Rotomagus: 'a lifetime as the raiders' harbour, where loot and captives are sold'. The edict of Pitres, 864, c. 25 forbids mail, arms and horses on pain of death, and does not name wine. Church plate is 240 d the piece (goods_793.json); the Dane sells it at a quarter. Sets nw_bought_loot.
cards.when: moored and port.id = rotomagus and year >= 856 and year < 911

clerk.name: Einold
clerk.note: rotomagus.einold, or the clerk after him

cards.title: The market on the mud
cards.intention: A fleet's quartermaster is selling on the mud under the wall what was taken upriver: plate, cloth and people. He takes silver by weight and wine by the cask.

options.label: Make up the clerk's silver and buy the deacon back
Buy the cup with the cross hammered flat
Sell him a cask for silver by weight
Walk on along the wall

cards.note: People: rotomagus.rollo (cast.rollo), a Frankish clerk who speaks for him. A lawsuit. The spine's hook for dorestad_falls at Rotomagus from 911: 'one lord, one toll, thieves hanged'. The rings on the oak and the hanging of thieves and of those who knew: Dudo of Saint-Quentin ii and William of Jumieges ii (LATER), retold as what people say. Telling him truly who is on the river is the story rotomagus.einolds_list, ending rollos_peace (sets df_warned; the toll eased).
cards.when: moored and port.id = rotomagus and year >= 911 and year < 931
cards.title: A cask from a guest's boat
cards.intention: In the night a cask was lifted out of your boat under the wall. This is Rollo's city now, with one lord and one law, and a theft from a guest can be laid before him in his hall.

options.label: Lay the theft before him
Answer his question first: tell him truly who is on the river behind you
Let the cask go and say nothing

memory.truth: told him truly who was on the river

cards.note: People: parisius.stephen (the count), parisius.dominicus (the abbey's toll man), parisius.fardulf named. A lawsuit: the story parisius.four_pennies. The count's agents asked four pennies a head of merchants at the fair until Pippin's judgment of 8 July 753 (Tardif no. 55); the charter of about 775 confirmed the abbey's tolls (Tardif no. 77). That the count's man still tries it in the 790s is the game's. Witness borne gives the freedom of the fair for three fairs (story/unlocks_793.json unlock_charter_parisius, as the places file's unlock parisius.freedom_of_the_fair has it).
cards.when: moored and port.id = parisius and year < 812 and month >= 10 and month <= 11 and not flag.nw_parisius_witness
cards.title: Four pennies a head
cards.intention: The count's court sits in his yard on the island. The abbey of Saint Denis complains that the count's man again asked four pennies a head from strangers at the fair, which King Pippin forbade forty years ago. You were at the landing, and the law-finders want a stranger's word.

options.label: Say what was asked of you at the landing
Say you were busy with your casks and heard nothing
Ask to hear King Pippin's judgment read before you answer

memory.witness: bore witness against the count's penny
memory.read: asked for the judgment to be read

cards.note: People: parisius.dominicus. The spine's hook for hungry_years and its flag hy_new_measure: the Synod of Frankfurt, June 794, c. 4 (the highest prices for oats, barley, rye and wheat, by the new public measure; chronicle_793.json 794-06-01-frankfurt-prices). The prices in his mouth are the capitulary's.
cards.when: moored and port.id = parisius and ((year = 794 and month >= 7) or year = 795 or year = 796) and not flag.hy_new_measure
cards.title: The king's measure
cards.intention: The king's ruling is cried at the saint's landing: the most that may be asked for a measure of oats, barley, rye and wheat, and one new measure for the whole realm. The abbey's toll man has the new measure and is setting every merchant's beside it.

options.label: Have your measure checked and marked
Buy a new measure from the abbey's cooper
Say a Frisian measure has served three generations

cards.note: People: parisius.waldric (cellarer of Saint-Denis), parisius.fardulf and parisius.stephen named. The spine's hook for hungry_years at Parisius (before 795): the abbeys feed hundreds at their gates. Sets hy_fed_poor or hy_sold_dear, as the story parisius.bread_at_the_gate has it. Wheat is 6 d the sack (goods_793.json); the king's price from June 794 is four pennies the measure; in a famine market it fetches three times its worth.
cards.when: moored and port.id = parisius and year < 795 and not flag.hy_sold_dear
cards.title: Bread at the gate
cards.intention: The abbey of Saint Denis is feeding hundreds at its gate and its barn is nearly empty. The cellarer will buy any grain at the abbey's price, which is low. In the island market the same sack fetches three times as much, and the count's men are watching who asks it.

options.label: Sell two sacks of wheat to the gate at the abbey's price
Sell the wheat in the island market for what it will fetch
Lend your crew to the ovens for a day

memory.gate: sold wheat to the gate at the abbey's price
memory.market: sold wheat dear in a hungry year
memory.baked: lent his crew to the ovens

cards.note: People: parisius.waldric; rotomagus.ursio (flag nw_ursio_debt, set at Rotomagus), rotomagus.schoolmaster named. The spine's hook for book_road: Saint-Denis buys parchment by the bundle at the October fair. A deal. Sets bk_parchment (he has sold parchment to a scriptorium, which gives the standing order) and bk_knows_worth. Parchment is 60 d the bundle of a hundred leaves; what the abbey passes over goes for fifty. The fair opens on Saint Denis's day, 9 October.
cards.when: moored and port.id = parisius and month >= 10 and month <= 11 and year < 816
cards.title: Skins by the bundle
cards.intention: At the fair of Saint Denis parchment is sold by the bundle of a hundred leaves. The abbey's cellarer goes from booth to booth, holds each leaf to the light and takes the best. What he passes over is good enough for a school.

options.label: Buy two bundles of what he passed over
Sell him the parchment you carry
Walk the booths with him and learn to judge a leaf
Tell him, where the abbot can hear, that Ursio of Rotomagus is still unpaid

memory.ursio: dunned him for the cooper before the abbot

cards.note: People: parisius.ermentrud (the widow by the Little Bridge), parisius.cellarer (Frotbald of Saint-Germain; cast here as 'germain', a monk, so as not to be taken for Saint-Denis's cellarer). A feast day: Martinmas, 11 November, when the sailing season ends and rents fall due (the spine's calendar). Tenants who owe wine to Saint-Germain are the matter of Abbot Irminon's book of estates (about 823-828); that her rent falls at Martinmas is the places file's.
cards.when: moored and port.id = parisius and feast and month = 11 and year < 823
cards.title: Martinmas rent
cards.intention: It is Martinmas. The tenants of Saint Germain's bring their wine rent to the abbey in the meadows, and the widow who lodges the Frisians has casks to cart and a carter who began the feast yesterday.

options.label: Roll her casks to the abbey with your crew
Keep the feast at her table
Ask the cellarer, quietly, for a cask of the rent wine

memory.carted: rolled her rent wine to the abbey

cards.note: People: parisius.ermentrud, cast.thiadbod (the Dorestad skipper: the tie is hers, 'lodged with her twenty Octobers and paid for nineteen; she holds one of his cloaks'). A favour. The short Frisian cloak is Notker I.34, retold. The price word (Frisian cloth short at the fair) is true while it lasts. Sets nw_thiadbod_cloak or nw_thiadbod_owes for whoever writes Thiadbod at Dorestad.
cards.when: moored and port.id = parisius and year < 823 and month >= 9 and month <= 11
cards.title: The twentieth October
cards.intention: The widow by the Little Bridge has lodged a Dorestad skipper twenty Octobers and been paid for nineteen. She holds one of his cloaks against the twentieth, and wants word carried to him.

options.label: Promise to tell him at Dorestad
Pay his twentieth October yourself
Sit down to the eel and hear what the Frisians said at her table

cards.note: People: the river man is forged; parisius.ermentrud 'knows where to hire a man who knows the river's bends'. A hire. The loops of the Seine below the city: the dossier (several days by water to Rotomagus). The card stops before the fleets of 845.
cards.when: moored and port.id = parisius and year < 845
cards.title: A man who knows the loops
cards.intention: On the strand under the island wall a river man with his own pole and no boat is looking for a berth. He says he knows every loop of the Seine down to the tide.

options.label: Take him on
Pay him to take you down to the tide and no further
Ask him the loops and what each costs

cards.note: People: parisius.fardulf (real: a Lombard, abbot of Saint-Denis 793-806, given the abbey for uncovering the plot of Pippin the Hunchback, Annales regni Francorum 792), rotomagus.hildhard (who has the psalter: the tie is in both files). A text wanted. The Rotomagus card harbour.rotomagus.owed_psalter is the middle of it. Sets bk_carried when the book comes home, bk_lost when it does not. His verses on the house he built for the king beside the abbey survive (MGH Poetae I), recalled from memory (?); the look of the psalter is invented.
cards.when: moored and port.id = parisius and year < 807 and not flag.nw_psalter_home
cards.title: The abbot's psalter
cards.intention: Abbot Fardulf of Saint Denis receives merchants who carry for the abbey. He asks every boat bound down the river the same thing: a psalter of the abbey's has been at Rotomagus for nine years, with the cathedral's chief singer.

options.label: Promise to ask at Rotomagus
Put the psalter into his hands
Tell him the psalter was in your boat and is gone
Hear the verses he has made for the king

memory.ask: promised to ask for the psalter

cards.note: The places file's easter egg at parisius.st_stephen. The carved pillar of the boatmen of the Parisii, set up to Jupiter under the emperor Tiberius, was found under the choir of Notre-Dame in 1711; its stones were built into the late Roman wall, so that men digging by the bishop's church could strike them at any time (the game's licence). The inscription says the boatmen set it up at their common cost. Nobody in 793 can know what it is.
cards.when: moored and port.id = parisius
cards.title: Boatmen in the stone
cards.intention: Men digging a footing by the bishop's church have struck carved stones deep under it: a row of men with shields, as in a boat, and a god with a stag's horns. A clerk is telling them to fill the hole.

options.label: Give the diggers a penny to leave it open till dusk
Help them fill it in
Say a prayer for all boatmen, theirs and yours

cards.note: People: the grower is forged. A deal. The port's goods: 'the wine, the honey and the dyers' roots' (the places file's summary). Madder is 12 d the sack and honey 24 d the crock (goods_793.json); he sells under, because his cart is borrowed.
cards.when: moored and port.id = parisius and month >= 8 and month <= 11
cards.title: The dyers' roots
cards.intention: A grower from up the river has madder roots dried and bagged, and the dyers he sells to have gone to the fair without him. He will sell cheap to a boat.

options.label: Buy three sacks of madder
Buy a crock of honey
Tell him where the dyers' booths stand at the fair

cards.note: People: parisius.abbo (real: Abbo of Saint-Germain, who saw the siege and wrote the Bella Parisiacae urbis), parisius.robert and his brother Count Odo named. The spine's hook for dorestad_falls at Parisius: the siege of 885-886. The flood that broke the Little Bridge on 6 February 886 and the twelve who held its tower: Abbo, Bella I. The names he recites are Abbo's own forms (Bella I; the Parisius dossier, section 3). The card runs from February 886, when the tower has burned. Sets the places file's flag parisius_stood. The boat lies above the bridges: the fleet holds the river below.
cards.when: moored and port.id = parisius and year = 886 and month >= 2 and month <= 10
cards.title: Under the tower
cards.intention: The Northmen's great fleet lies below the bridges and the city is shut. A young monk on the wall wants to know who you are and where you stood. The count's men want two things: grain brought in from above, and word carried out.

options.label: Sell the count your wheat
Carry the count's word out by the upper river
Hear the twelve names

memory.grain: brought wheat into the besieged city
memory.word: carried word out of the siege
memory.names: heard the names of the twelve

cards.note: People: namnetis.nanthard (the toll man); the pilgrim is forged; namnetis.gunhard named from 835. A feast day: Saint John the Baptist, 24 June, with its vigil the night before (the port's seasons; pilgrims 'from far cities' on the feast: Chronicon Namnetense c. 5-6). Traders passing as pilgrims is King Charles's complaint to Offa in 796. The card stops before the feast of 843.
cards.when: moored and port.id = namnetis and feast and month = 6 and year < 843

tollman.name: Nanthard
tollman.note: namnetis.nanthard, and the toll man after him

cards.title: Saint John's eve
cards.intention: It is Saint John's feast. Pilgrims have come in from far cities, the night before is a vigil at his church by the cathedral, and every gate of the city stands open.

options.label: Keep the vigil at the saint's church with your crew
Sell to the pilgrims from the boat
Let pilgrims sleep aboard for a penny each

memory.sold: sold to pilgrims on the feast

cards.note: People: namnetis.eadhelm (invented English monk of Saint Martin's at Tours), cast.alcuin, cast.sigewine and burdigala.placidina named (flag nw_poets_copy, set at Burdigala; nw_sigewine_carried, set at Quentovic). A commission. The spine's hook for book_road at Namnetis (796-843): the way up the Loire to Tours, skins going up and books coming down. Calfskin is carried as cattle_hides (15 d the bundle; goods_793.json). The copy of the Bordeaux poet is the story burdigala.poets_book, ending copy_to_tours (sets bk_carried). Sets bk_knows_worth.
cards.when: moored and port.id = namnetis and year >= 796 and year < 827
cards.title: Skins for Tours
cards.intention: On the island of Indre below the city an English monk of Saint Martin's at Tours buys calfskins for the abbey's scribes and looks for boats to carry finished books north. He is exact about books and hopeless about boats.

options.label: Take his order for calfskin: eight bundles of hides
Sell him the hides you carry
Hand him the copy of the Bordeaux poet
options.check: flag.nw_poets_copy and not flag.nw_poets_home and hold.books > 0

options.label: Ask him what a book is worth, and to whom

memory.hides: sold him hides for the scribes
memory.poet: brought the poet's book for Tours
memory.worth: asked what a book is worth

cards.note: People: namnetis.pilot (Paternus the ferryman), namnetis.wido (the count). The story namnetis.names_on_the_spears: in 799 Count Wido rode through all Brittany and brought the king the weapons of the chiefs who yielded, each with its owner's name (Annales regni Francorum 799). The ferryman's kin and the salt masters of Batz are the game's. Sets nw_namnetis_straight or nw_namnetis_counts_ear.
cards.when: moored and port.id = namnetis and year >= 799 and year < 802 and not flag.nw_namnetis_straight and not flag.nw_namnetis_counts_ear
cards.title: A name in the cart
cards.intention: Count Wido has ridden through all Brittany and come home with a cart of the chiefs' weapons, each cut with its owner's name, to lay before the king. The list was read aloud in the count's yard. The ferryman at the Reze crossing asks whether a certain name was in it.

options.label: Tell him the list as you heard it
Tell the count that the ferryman is asking
Say you were watching your casks, not listening

memory.count: told the count he was asking
memory.silent: would not say what was read

cards.note: People: namnetis.electa (the ale-wife), namnetis.nanthard, namnetis.eadhelm (he owes her for his carters: the tie in the file). A rumour that is true: who is about to sell salt cheap (the price at Namnetis falls for some weeks). Salt comes up from the bay from the Assumption to Saint Luke's day (the port's seasons).
cards.when: moored and port.id = namnetis and year < 824
cards.title: The beam of chalk strokes
cards.intention: The ale-house by the carters' gate keeps every salt man's reckoning in chalk strokes on a beam. Its keeper knows who owes whom in the port, and who is about to sell cheap because of it.

options.label: Ask which salt masters are selling cheap
Pay off the English monk's carters from her beam
options.check: year >= 796 and silver >= 5 and not flag.nw_eadhelm_debt_paid

options.label: Drink on the beam and settle when you sail

memory.salt: asked who was selling salt cheap

cards.note: People: namnetis.gunhard (real: bishop 835-843, killed at his altar on Saint John's day 843, Chronicon Namnetense c. 5-6), rotomagus.einold (his letter: flag nw_einold_letter). The story namnetis.saint_johns_day: the Northmen broke in 'by the old doorway' that had long been blocked (Chronicon Namnetense c. 6). Sets the spine's df_warned (he brought warning before it came) and nw_namnetis_doorway. A hundred pennies is a part of the work namnetis.work.doorway, not the whole of it.
cards.when: moored and port.id = namnetis and (year = 841 or year = 842 or (year = 843 and month <= 6)) and not flag.nw_namnetis_doorway
cards.title: The stopped doorway
cards.intention: Bishop Gunhard takes you to see an old doorway in the city wall, stopped long ago with loose rubble. He asks what you saw on the Rhine: how long there is between the first sail and the fire.

options.label: Tell him plainly: less than a morning
Give a hundred pennies toward masons for the doorway
Say the Loire is wider than the Rhine and the count has men

memory.told: told him how fast a fleet comes
memory.masons: paid toward walling the old doorway

cards.note: People: the sons of burdigala.natan (invented; Jews are named at Bordeaux once, in 848, Annales Bertiniani, and the annal's charge against them is never told as fact: the Burdigala file). Scheduled by harbour.burdigala.nine_and_a_chest; the story burdigala.three_tellings, ending carried_them_out, and the unlock burdigala.natans_word. Sets nw_natans_word (a factor's welcome at Namnetis: see 'needs', there is no unlock_factor_namnetis).
cards.when: moored and port.id = namnetis and flag.nw_natan_carried and not flag.nw_natans_word
cards.title: Natan's sons
cards.intention: Nine people of Bordeaux and a chest of scrolls came ashore here from your boat. The city they left has burned. The sons of the man who paid you with a promise have come down to the port to keep it.

options.label: Take the silver
Take half, and leave half with them to trade for your house

memory.half: left half the debt with them as a stake

cards.note: People: the canons of Nantes; herio.martinus named. Scheduled by harbour.herio.clerk_in_the_hut. After the storming of Nantes on 24 June 843 the fleet shared its plunder on Herio and fought over it; some captives escaped, one with the cathedral's Bible (the Namnetis file: 'one with the cathedral's great Bible hung on his neck', Chronicon Namnetense c. 7). The cathedral was cleansed by Bishop Susan of Vannes on its dedication day, 30 September (c. 7). The story herio.whoever_holds, ending book_home: 300 pennies from the canons, paid over two years (half is paid here).
cards.when: moored and port.id = namnetis and flag.herio_bible_home and not flag.nw_bible_thanked
cards.title: The book on the altar
cards.intention: The cathedral of Nantes has been washed of blood and Mass is said in it again. The great Bible that went downriver on a captive's neck lies on the altar, salt-stained along one edge. The canons have sent for the master of the boat that brought it.

options.label: Take what the canons can pay
Tell them to put it toward buying their people back

memory.took: was paid for bringing the Bible home
memory.forgave: gave the Bible's reward to the ransom

cards.note: People: herio.cellarer (Vitalis), herio.maura (the rakers on the sand), burdigala.oil_seller (Felix: flag nw_herio_lamps is read at Burdigala). The story herio.three_lamps and the spine's thread hungry_years (sets hy_fed_poor when corn is sold to the house at its price). The three lamps at the founder's tomb and the oil ship from Bordeaux: Vita Filiberti (dossiers/herio.md). Salt is 3 d the sack, rye 4, oil 40 the jar: his rate in salt is one no mainland market gives.
cards.when: moored and port.id = herio and year < 796
cards.title: Oil for three lamps
cards.intention: The island has salt and little else this hungry year. The corn sacks in the cellarer's store hang slack, the oil ship from Bordeaux has not come, and three lamps have burned at the founder's head since he died.

options.label: Sell him two sacks of rye for salt
Sell him a jar of oil for salt
Sell the rye to the rakers on the sand, who offer more
Promise him oil from Bordeaux

memory.rye: sold corn to the house in a hungry year
memory.sand: sold corn on the sand over his head

cards.note: People: herio.natalis (the salt brother), quentovic.meginbert (who sent the leaf), herio.adalard, mogontia.folcbald (who keeps the next). A riddle and a text given: Aldhelm's wine cask (riddles_793.json riddle_aldhelm_78_cupa_vinaria, given by 'a monk of the salt pans' at Herio, 793-835; texts_793.json aldhelm_78_cupa_vinaria), the second leaf of the set salt_to_pepper. The clues are our own rendering. After 835 the leaf is at Namnetis (the places files).
cards.when: moored and port.id = herio and year < 836
cards.title: The salt brother
cards.intention: The brother who keeps the salt will not hand over a sack without setting a riddle first. He has a leaf sent from Quentovic, the second of four, and gives it only to someone who has answered the first.

options.label: Answer the salt riddle
Answer the cask riddle
Guess, wrongly, and buy salt at the common price

memory.answered: answered the salt riddle on the pans

cards.note: People: herio.adalard (real: Adalard of Corbie, Charlemagne's cousin, exiled to the island 814-821; cast here as 'abbot', which he is, of Corbie), the watcher at the door (the game's), namnetis.wido (the count who pays for knowing), quentovic.corbie_agent. The story herio.emperors_cousin, first step. Sets nw_adalard_letter (the Quentovic card harbour.quentovic.corbies_man follows), nw_adalard_informed or nw_adalard_done.
cards.when: moored and port.id = herio and year >= 814 and year < 821 and not flag.nw_adalard_letter and not flag.nw_adalard_done
cards.title: The emperor's cousin
cards.intention: The old emperor's cousin, Abbot Adalard of Corbie, lives in the island's guest house as the new emperor's exile, with a king's man by the door. On the second evening, while the watcher eats, he asks whether your boat calls at Quentovic.

options.label: Take the letter for Quentovic
Take it, and tell the watcher
Tell him plainly you will not carry it

memory.informed: showed the exile's letter to the watcher

cards.note: People: herio.adalard, quentovic.corbie_agent, cast.anskar named. The story herio.emperors_cousin, last step: he weighs the book in his hand before he opens it, and reads the first page standing. Sets the spine's bk_carried and bk_knows_worth, or bk_lost. The unlock herio.adalards_word follows from nw_adalard_done with bk_carried.
cards.when: moored and port.id = herio and flag.nw_adalard_book and not flag.nw_adalard_done and year < 822
cards.title: A book the length of a hand
cards.intention: The exile has seen your sail from the guest-house window. He is at the west gate before you are, and the watcher is a little way behind him.

options.label: Give him the book
Give him the book, and ask what is in it
Tell him it is gone

memory.asked: brought the book and asked what it said

cards.note: People: herio.maura (the widow who leads the rakers; she 'knows who has a son who wants to go to sea'); the lad is forged. A hire and a deal. The islanders with a lord of their own, not the monks' people: Ermentarius, Miracula I.1. Iron tools are 30 d the crate and salt 3 d the sack (goods_793.json).
cards.when: moored and port.id = herio and year < 827
cards.title: On the sand
cards.intention: On the sand by the salt heaps the islanders trade for what the monks do not buy: needles, knives, cloth, a pot. The widow who leads the rakers has a neighbour's son beside her who wants to go to sea.

options.label: Trade a crate of iron tools for salt
Take the lad on
Let her show you which heap is which

memory.hired: took an island lad to sea

cards.note: People: herio.martinus (the islander who stayed), a clerk of Nantes (namnetis.gunhard's church). The story herio.whoever_holds: after Saint John's day 843 the fleet shares the loot of Nantes on Herio and fights over it (Chronicon Namnetense c. 7); a captive escapes at low water with the cathedral's Bible on his neck (the Namnetis file). Sets the Herio file's flag herio_bible_home and the spine's bk_carried, and schedules harbour.namnetis.book_on_the_altar; or nw_herio_loot. Church plate is 240 d the piece; they sell it by weight at a sixth. Salt doubles on the Seine and the Canche while the Loire is shut.
cards.when: moored and port.id = herio and year = 843 and month >= 6 and month <= 9 and not flag.herio_bible_home and not flag.nw_herio_loot
cards.title: The clerk in the salt hut
cards.intention: The fleet that stormed Nantes on Saint John's day lies in the shell bay, sharing its plunder on the sand and fighting over it. In the salt hut, under the rakes, the islander is hiding a clerk of the cathedral with its great Bible strapped to his body.

options.label: Take the clerk and the book off on the night ebb
Buy altar plate in the bay, by weight
Load salt on the lagoon side and ask nothing

memory.took: took the clerk and the Bible off the island

cards.note: People: herio.ursus (the bay pilot), burdigala.amantius (his friend at the Garonne mouth, never met: the tie in both files; flag nw_herio_piloted is read at Burdigala). Ships lie windbound at Conca and are fed for charity (the port's eras; the work herio.work.windbound_dole). The channel to the monastery dries twice a day; a flat summer sea is a road for anyone (the king's council of 836, Ermentarius, Miracula I.1).
cards.when: moored and port.id = herio and year < 822
cards.title: Windbound at Conca
cards.intention: Ships lie in the shell bay waiting for a wind, fed by the monks for charity. The island's pilot sits on an upturned boat watching the water, and says the channel to the monastery dries twice a day.

options.label: Hire him over the bar on the next flood
Wait for the wind with the others and share the monks' bread
Ask him to name the marks, and say them back

memory.waited: waited for the wind at Conca

cards.note: People: burdigala.amantius (the pilot), burdigala.seguin (who owes him three seasons), herio.ursus (flag nw_herio_piloted: the bread and the insult). A hundred kilometres of tidal river and banks between the city and the sea: 'he comes with a pilot or not at all' (the places file). The wave that runs up the river ahead of the flood at the big tides of the low river is known from later centuries (?).
cards.when: moored and port.id = burdigala and year < 825
cards.title: The pilot's fee
cards.intention: The old pilot who brought you through the banks of the river mouth is waiting at the gate. He has piloted the count's boats for three seasons on a promise, and would like his fee from you in silver, before you sell.

options.label: Pay him at the gate
Pay him, and two pennies over for his grandson to teach you the marks
Promise to pay when the cargo is sold

memory.paid: paid the pilot at the gate
memory.marks: paid for the marks of the river

cards.note: People: burdigala.placidina (the widow of the house by the Broken Tower), namnetis.eadhelm and cast.alcuin (who want a copy: the ties in both files). A text wanted. The story burdigala.poets_book: the book is Ausonius's, and her lines are our own rendering of his verses on Bordeaux in the Ordo urbium nobilium (walls four-square, towers that pierce the clouds, the ocean's tide bringing a sea of fleets up the river). Sets nw_poets_copy; the Namnetis card harbour.namnetis.skins_for_tours takes the copy for Tours. A book is 360 d: the copy costs its skins.
cards.when: moored and port.id = burdigala and year < 829
cards.title: The poet of the city
cards.intention: The widow who keeps the house by the Broken Tower has one old book: the verses a man of this city made when Rome still ruled, about Bordeaux and every other famous city. On a slow evening she reads from it to the room.

options.label: Listen to the end
Pay for the copy and carry it to the Loire
options.check: year >= 796 and silver >= 40 and not flag.nw_poets_copy

options.label: Tell her the news of the Loire and the Franks

memory.listened: heard the poet read to the end
memory.copy: paid for a copy of the poet's book
memory.news: brought her news of the Loire

cards.note: People: burdigala.oil_seller (Felix, invented), herio.cellarer (Vitalis, who owes him: the tie in both files; flag nw_herio_lamps is set on the island). The story herio.three_lamps: the oil comes up from the south by river and cart and is dear this year. Oil is 40 d the jar (goods_793.json). The island pays in salt (harbour.herio.three_lamps) and in the commission it posts.
cards.when: moored and port.id = burdigala and year < 800
cards.title: Oil for the island
cards.intention: Oil comes up from the south by river and cart and is dear this year. The seller knows the island of the three lamps: its monks owe him for last year's jars, and no oil ship has gone north.

options.label: Buy two jars outright
Stand surety for the monks, and carry four jars on their account
Ask what he would give for bay salt

memory.surety: stood surety for the island's oil

cards.note: People: burdigala.seguin (real: the count set over Bordeaux in 778, the Astronomer c. 3; probably the Seguin put out in 816; that he holds the city in 793 is not recorded (?)), namnetis.wido (his rival: the tie in both files; the cart of 799). The places file's unlock burdigala.counts_leave: leave to trade across the river with the Gascons, for a gift and an audience, lost if arms go across (the capitulary of Herstal, 779, forbids mail out of the realm). Sets nw_burdigala_leave.
cards.when: moored and port.id = burdigala and year < 817
cards.title: The count's leave
cards.intention: Count Seguin holds the city for King Louis and the river against the Gascons on the far bank. Nobody trades across the water without his leave, and he gives it for a gift, for news of the king, or not at all.

options.label: Give him a gift for his leave
Tell him where the king is, and what the Franks say in the north
Ask what a horse fetches south of the Loire

memory.gift: gave a gift for leave to trade across the river
memory.horse: asked the price of a horse

cards.note: People: burdigala.natan (invented wine and salt dealer). A passenger to carry. The story burdigala.three_tellings: the Danes lie round the wall through 847 and the city is taken by night early in 848 (Annales Bertiniani 847, 848; the Chronicle of Fontenelle). The annal's line that Jews betrayed the city is one distant bishop's and is never told as fact (the Burdigala file's caution): the card shows only a household that has read enough to know who will be blamed. Schedules harbour.namnetis.natans_sons. Wine at a third of its 45 d.
cards.when: moored and port.id = burdigala and (year = 847 or (year = 848 and month <= 3)) and not flag.nw_natan_carried
cards.title: Nine people and a chest
cards.intention: The Danes have lain round the wall for months. At the water gate a wine and salt dealer of the city asks passage to the Loire for nine people and a chest of scrolls. He will pay in wine, in silver, or in a debt his sons will honour. Others at the gate watch whom you take.

options.label: Take the nine and the chest out on the night ebb
Buy his wine at a third and run it out alone
Tell him your boat is too small for nine

memory.carried: carried his household out of the siege
memory.wine: bought his wine in the siege
